title: 艺术与审美：建筑怎么看
title_en: Art & Aesthetics: How to Look at Architecture

questions.question: 有人说「看一座建筑，拍一张漂亮的正面照就够了」。按「建筑是用脚和身体读的」这一看法，这种做法漏掉了什么？
options: 建筑师在图纸上给每个房间设定的功能分区
建筑的绝对尺寸，越高大越能体现艺术价值
立面装饰的精细程度，以及外墙所用材料是否足够昂贵
人走进、穿过时依次展开的空间序列，如先压后放
questions.explanation: 建筑是「时间的艺术」，真正的艺术在走进去、穿过去的过程里发生——低矮门廊接豁然开朗的大厅，身体先于大脑感到。立面只是封面；贵材料、一味求大也都被文章明确列为误区。
questions.question_en: Someone says one good photo of a building's façade is enough to appreciate it. If architecture is read with your feet and body, what does that miss?
options_en: The functional zoning the architect assigned to each room on the plans
The building's absolute size, since bigger means greater artistic value
How finely the façade is ornamented and how costly its materials are
The sequence of spaces that unfolds as you walk in and through, such as compression followed by release
questions.explanation_en: Architecture is an art of time: it happens as you move through it, as when a low porch gives way to a soaring hall and the body feels it before the mind does. The façade is just the cover, and expensive materials and sheer size are both named as misconceptions.

questions.question: 许多神圣空间宁可整体昏暗，只在关键处放一束光。按「光是建筑的材料」这一思路，这样做的道理是？
options: 受当时的建造技术所限开不了大窗，昏暗只是不得已的结果
昏暗能让人看不清结构，从而掩盖建造上的粗糙
采光越暗越节能，神圣空间更讲究朴素节俭
明暗配合能引导脚步和情绪，留暗让那束光更有力量
questions.explanation: 建筑里的光讲究怎么进来、什么形状、和暗怎么搭：通道做暗、圣坛做亮，人就被光「领着」往前走。处处通亮往往最没气氛；哥特教堂靠飞扶壁恰恰开出了大片花窗，说明昏暗并非技术无奈。
questions.question_en: Many sacred spaces stay mostly dim and place a single shaft of light where it matters. If light is treated as a building material, why do this?
options_en: Builders of the time couldn't make large windows, so dimness was simply unavoidable
Dimness hides the structure so that rough construction goes unnoticed
Dimmer spaces save energy, and sacred buildings favor frugality
Pairing dark and light steers your steps and emotions; the darkness makes that one beam far more powerful
questions.explanation_en: What matters is how light enters, its shape, and how it plays against darkness: a dark passage and a bright altar lead you forward. Uniform brightness usually kills atmosphere, and Gothic builders used flying buttresses precisely to open huge windows, so dimness wasn't a technical limitation.

questions.question: 哥特教堂的飞扶壁、中国木构的斗栱，常被当作建筑最好看的部分。这体现了看建筑的哪条原则？
options: 真正的好建筑应把受力构件都藏起来，只露出光洁平整的表面
结构为受力而生，诚实地露出来，本身就成了装饰和美
贵重材料和繁复雕饰，是建筑之美的主要来源
装饰与结构各管各的，好看的部分往往与承重无关
questions.explanation: 飞扶壁把屋顶的侧推力引到地面，墙才敢开大窗；斗栱把屋檐重量传下来，同时极有韵律。它们本来都为受力而生，却成了最好看的地方——「结构变成了装饰」。文章也明确反对「贵材料＝好建筑」。
questions.question_en: The flying buttresses of Gothic cathedrals and the dougong brackets of Chinese timber buildings are often their most beautiful features. Which principle does this illustrate?
options_en: Good buildings should hide their load-bearing members behind smooth, clean surfaces
Structure born of load-bearing needs, honestly exposed, becomes ornament and beauty in itself
Precious materials and elaborate carving are the main source of architectural beauty
Ornament and structure are separate; the beautiful parts usually have nothing to do with support
questions.explanation_en: Flying buttresses carry the roof's outward thrust to the ground so walls can open into vast windows; dougong transfer the eaves' weight while forming a rhythmic pattern. Both exist for structural reasons yet became the most beautiful parts — structure as ornament. The piece explicitly rejects the idea that expensive materials make good architecture.
